title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page has nothing to do with the crystal and F-crystal computations on the neighbouring pages (Frobenius Φ, connection matrix A, dΦ = Φ∘A^σ − A∘Φ). It is a self-contained sketch in elementary differential topology: submanifolds and the atlases of 'slice' or 'adapted' charts that describe them.

Top-left drawing. A large region Φ_m (an m-manifold) contains a long wiggling curve Φ_n (an n-dimensional subset winding back and forth). A small neighbourhood U of a point is singled out, with V the part of Φ_n inside it. A map σ sends U to R^m, and R^n sits inside R^m. The labels C^1, (C^0), ∅, C^{r-1}, 'm-n' and 'n-1' record the smoothness classes and codimensions being considered.

The wiggling picture illustrates the danger the definition must exclude. For an immersed (or dense, accumulating) submanifold, the chart neighbourhood U meets Φ_n in more than the single sheet V.

Defining condition. A chart pair (σ, (U, V)) with V ⊂ U must satisfy σ(V) = σ(U) ∩ R^n. This is the standard submanifold-chart (slice-chart) condition.

Atlas. A_0 = {(σ_i, (U_i, V_i))} is an atlas of class C^r of such pairs, with V_i ⊂ U_i.

Typology of 'families' (Grothendieck's word for these atlases), with smoothness classes:
1) canonical families, C^r, r ≥ 0;
2) regular (quasi-regular) families, C^r, r ≥ 1;
3) natural families, r ≥ 1;
4) normal families, r ≥ 1.
Items 3 and 4 are bracketed together with C^{r-1}. This matches the familiar loss of one derivative when passing to tangent or normal data: a C^r submanifold has a C^{r-1} normal bundle and C^{r-1} tubular structures.

Bottom of the page: compatibility of two chart pairs (σ_1,(U_1,V_1)) and (σ_2,(U_2,V_2)), with a picture of two overlapping disks around a curve and their images in R^m meeting R^n.
- One requires V_1 ∩ V_2 ≠ ∅.
- One restricts both charts to (U_1∩U_2, V_1∩V_2), giving σ'_1 and σ'_2.
- One needs the conditions U_1 ∩ V_2 = V_1 ∩ V_2 and U_2 ∩ V_1 = V_1 ∩ V_2. These say that the sheets are locally the full trace of the subspace, i.e. V_i = U_i ∩ N.

The page thus sets up axioms for a 'manifold together with a submanifold' via an atlas of pairs. The four kinds of families are presumably increasingly rigid structures along the submanifold, down to normal or tubular data of class C^{r-1}.
errors: No genuine errors. Note that the overlap conditions U_1∩V_2 = V_1∩V_2 are automatic if V_i = U_i ∩ N for a fixed embedded N. They are needed only when the V_i are given abstractly; the wiggly picture shows why, since the condition fails for immersed or dense submanifolds.
The definitions of 'canonical/regular/natural/normal families' are only named, not given, so they cannot be checked.

ideas.what: Slice-chart atlas of pairs (σ,(U,V)) with σ(V)=σ(U)∩R^n describing an embedded submanifold, with compatibility on overlaps
ideas.modern_name: submanifold (slice) charts / adapted atlas for a pair (M,N)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Whitney, Ehresmann era; standard textbook material)

ideas.what: Hierarchy of structures along a C^r submanifold with loss of one derivative (C^{r-1}) for 'natural'/'normal' families
ideas.modern_name: normal bundle / tubular neighbourhood structures of class C^{r-1}

ideas.what: Picture of an immersed/dense curve in a manifold as a counterexample to slice charts

deep.surprise_reason: These are elementary differential-topology notes on submanifold atlases, possibly taken while listening to a talk or helping someone, interleaved with crystal computations. The material is standard; the only mild curiosity is Grothendieck engaging with C^r differential topology around 1970.
transcription_corrections: The label transcribed 'C^∞ [?]' near the top is more likely 'C^{r-1}' (written vertically).
In the formula A_0 = {(σ_i,(U_i,V_i))} the class label at right is 'C^r'.
The drawing at top-left shows Φ_n as a wiggling (immersed or accumulating) curve inside Φ_m, with U a small disk around a point of V; the arrow σ goes to R^m ⊃ R^n.
